notes: Compare two ways of doing a job. Tick Compare two ways of doing it, name the two options, and tag each hire and each rebilled cost with the one it belongs to - anything left on Both is shared. The quote then prints the services and the crew once, because they are the same either way, and gives each option its own kit, its own logistics, its own share of the production fee and its own bottom line. The fee follows each option rather than being typed once, so bringing your own kit shows a smaller fee than hiring locally, which is usually the point of the comparison. Press They chose this and the other option's lines are removed and the job goes back to being an ordinary job. Hires and expenses can be priced in another currency: pick EUR or one of the others, give the rate you got, and the quote and invoice show sterling with the original beside it - 2 x 3 days x 900 euro a day at 1.17. The profit figures use the converted cost. Dates that are not consecutive no longer print as a range: a job on the 1st and the 20th said 1st-20th August, which read as twenty days and contradicted the opening line of the same email; it now lists them. And the app no longer dies on a single unreadable job. One bad row used to stop it loading at all, leaving every job stranded in storage; rows are read one at a time now, anything unreadable is set aside and written back untouched rather than lost, and the list says so instead of quietly being short.
